title: What the mind holds at the very end

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकिं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम । अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O Supreme Person, what is Brahman? What is the self? What is action? What is called the field of changing things, and what is called the divine principle? What is the sacred offering here in this body, and how are you known at the time of death by those with disciplined minds?
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna now asks Krishna to define the deepest terms behind life, death, and the imperishable reality. Listen to the five questions he fires off.

body.text: Arjuna says: O Supreme Person, what is Brahman? What is the self? What is action? What is called the field of changing things, and what is called the divine principle? What is the sacred offering here in this body, and how are you known at the time of death by those with disciplined minds? Arjuna calls Krishna Purushottama, the Supreme Person, and fires off a string of five what questions. The Sanskrit repeats kim, what, five times, turning the verse into a single, urgent demand for definitions. Arjuna asks who the sacrifice is inside the body and how Krishna is known at the moment of death. This verse answers what Brahman and the other terms are.

verses.sa: अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन । प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O Madhusudana, who is the sacrifice here, and how does he dwell in this body? And at the time of death, how are you known by those with disciplined minds?
verses.angle: Adhiyajna: the inner lord of sacrifice
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna asks Krishna to name the inner ruler of sacrifice, and to explain how a disciplined mind knows him at the moment of death.

body.text: Arjuna says: O Madhusudana, who is the sacrifice here, and how does he dwell in this body? And at the time of death, how are you known by those with disciplined minds? Arjuna asks about adhiyajna, the lord of sacrifice, and where that presence lives: inside the body. He wants to know how the self, the body, and the sacrifice fit together. Krishna answers that the imperishable is the supreme reality and one's own nature is the inner self.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते । भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥
verses.tr: The imperishable is the supreme reality. One's own nature is called the inner self. The offering that brings beings into existence is called action.
verses.angle: Aksharam, imperishable, is the supreme reality
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna begins to answer by naming three things. Listen for how he defines the imperishable reality, the inner self, and the act that creates life.

body.text: The imperishable is the supreme reality. One's own nature is called the inner self. The offering that brings beings into existence is called action. Krishna names three things in one breath. First, the imperishable, aksharam, is the supreme reality, Brahman. Then he says your own nature, svabhavah, is the inner self, adhyatma. Finally, the offering that brings beings into existence is called action. Krishna now turns to the body and the cosmic person, showing how the perishable and the radiant meet. He says I am the inner witness in this body, Arjuna.

verses.sa: अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् । अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥
verses.tr: The perishable world is the lower realm; the cosmic person is the radiant being. I am the inner witness of sacrifice in this body, Arjuna.
verses.angle: I indeed am the inner witness of sacrifice here
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now answers Arjuna's question about the terms needed for dying with awareness. Listen for the three things he names.

body.text: The perishable world is the lower realm; the cosmic person is the radiant being. I am the inner witness of sacrifice in this body, Arjuna. Krishna calls himself the inner witness of sacrifice inside the body, adhhiyajna, and says this is true for every embodied being, var. He then says that whoever remembers him at the end and leaves the body attains his state.

verses.sa: अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् । यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥
verses.tr: Whoever remembers Me at the end and leaves the body attains My state; there is no doubt.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the sacred act and the cosmic person. Now he gives the final promise.

body.text: Whoever remembers Me at the end and leaves the body attains My state; there is no doubt. Whoever remembers Krishna at the end and leaves the body reaches his state, he says, without doubt. Krishna now explains why the state a person remembers is exactly the state they reach.

verses.sa: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥
verses.tr: Whatever state a person remembers at the end, that state is reached, because the mind has been shaped by it.
verses.angle: Bhavabhavitah, formed by that state, means a life of repeated practice
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: If you remember Me at death, you reach Me, Krishna said in the last verse. But what if you remember something else? Here is the answer.

body.text: Whatever state a person remembers at the end, that state is reached, because the mind has been shaped by it. Krishna does not say the final thought is a sudden accident. He says the mind is always formed by that state, meaning the final thought is simply the deepest habit of a lifetime. Krishna then tells Arjuna to make that habit of remembering Him his daily practice.

verses.sa: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, remember Me at all times and fight. With mind and intellect offered to Me, you will surely come to Me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has taught that the final thought shapes the final destination. Now he gives Arjuna two commands together.

body.text: Therefore, remember Me at all times and fight. With mind and intellect offered to Me, you will surely come to Me. Notice the pairing in this verse. Krishna commands Arjuna to remember Me at all times and to fight. Remembrance and action are not separate. Krishna then explains that the final thought at the moment of death determines the final destination.

verses.sa: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना । परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥
verses.tr: One who departs while remembering the divine person with a mind trained by practice and fixed on nothing else reaches that supreme divine being, O Partha.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen closely for one word, and you will hear how Krishna describes the exact state of mind that reaches the supreme divine at the moment of death.

body.text: One who departs while remembering the divine person with a mind trained by practice and fixed on nothing else reaches that supreme divine being, O Partha. Listen for nanyagamina, meaning not going elsewhere. A mind trained by steady practice and fixed on nothing else reaches the supreme person at the moment of death. Krishna turns to the nature of the supreme person, who is beyond thought and radiant like the sun.

verses.sa: कविं पुराणमनुशासितारमणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः । सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपमादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ॥
verses.tr: Whoever remembers the wise, ancient, ruler, subtler than the subtle, supporter of all, beyond thought, radiant like the sun, and beyond darkness...
verses.angle: Anushastaram: the ruler of the self
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has learned how to fix his mind at the moment of death. Now Krishna describes the reality he is meant to hold in mind. Listen to how the divine is defined.

body.text: Whoever remembers the wise, ancient, ruler, subtler than the subtle, supporter of all, beyond thought, radiant like the sun, and beyond darkness... This verse names the divine as anushastaram, the ruler. This is not a king of a land, but the ruler of the self, the one who governs the inner life. Krishna now explains the exact physical and mental steps one must take at the moment of death to reach that ruler.

verses.sa: प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेनभक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव । भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक्स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥
verses.tr: At the time of departure, one who leaves the body with an unmoving mind, devotion, and the power of yoga, placing the life-force between the eyebrows, reaches the divine supreme person.
verses.angle: bhruvor madhye, the place of departure
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries on from the supreme person's light, and now he asks what inner state carries a person to that same light at departure.

body.text: At the time of departure, one who leaves the body with an unmoving mind, devotion, and the power of yoga, placing the life-force between the eyebrows, reaches the divine supreme person. Listen to the exact place, bhruvor madhye, between the eyebrows. This is where the life-force is drawn up, and from here the soul departs. He now names the imperishable state that the knowers of the Vedas call deathless.

verses.sa: यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्तिविशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः । यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्तितत्ते पदं संग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥
verses.tr: I will briefly tell you that imperishable state, which the knowers of the Vedas call imperishable, which the detached ascetics enter, and which seekers follow through celibate discipline.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: What is the imperishable state that sages seek and describe? Krishna promises to answer this question in one verse.

body.text: I will briefly tell you that imperishable state, which the knowers of the Vedas call imperishable, which the detached ascetics enter, and which seekers follow through celibate discipline. The verse repeats one word, aksharam, the imperishable. It is the same object that Vedic scholars name, detached ascetics enter, and celibate seekers pursue, binding all three paths to a single goal. Krishna then closes the senses and fixes the mind, giving the exact method to reach that imperishable state.

verses.sa: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च । मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥
verses.tr: Closing all the doors of the senses, holding the mind in the heart, and placing the life-force in the head, one remains fixed in yoga-discipline.
verses.angle: Samyamy: the first act of closing sense-doors
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from the goal to the method of departure. He gives a precise sequence of three acts to master the body at death.

body.text: Closing all the doors of the senses, holding the mind in the heart, and placing the life-force in the head, one remains fixed in yoga-discipline. Listen to the word murdhni, the head. Krishna directs the life-force to be placed there, making the head the seat of his final yoga-discipline. He adds that uttering Om and remembering Him is the final step that seals this departure.

verses.sa: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् । यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
verses.tr: Uttering Om, the one-syllable Brahman, and remembering Me, one who departs while leaving the body attains the supreme state.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for the sound that Krishna says is the one-syllable form of the absolute, and how it is joined to his own name at the final moment.

body.text: Uttering Om, the one-syllable Brahman, and remembering Me, one who departs while leaving the body attains the supreme state. The single syllable Om is called Brahman, the one-syllable absolute. It is not a mere sound, but the ultimate reality, and it is to be spoken while Krishna is remembered. Krishna then tells Arjuna that for one who constantly remembers him, he is easy to reach.
